pll2d6c7-d1e3514.summary: States that others, defeated by saints living justly and chastely, seem to lose the power to tempt others.
claims: Defeated demons may lose power to tempt.

pll2d6c7-d1e3517.summary: Cites Origen: saints who resist and conquer these instigators diminish the demons' army, as if killing many, and a spirit defeated by a saint living chastely may not attack another.
claims: Saints diminish the demons' power by victory.

pll2d6c7-d1e3532.summary: Reports that some understand this only of the vice in which the demon was defeated: if defeated tempting to pride, it may no longer tempt anyone to pride.
claims: The restriction may apply only to the specific vice.

pl-l2d6c7.summary: Adds that demons defeated by saints living justly and chastely seem to lose the power to tempt others. Origen: saints who resist and conquer these instigators diminish the army of demons, and a spirit conquered by a chaste saint may not attack another person. Some think this applies only to the vice in which the demon was defeated.
claims: Demons defeated by saints seem to lose the power to tempt others.
Saints who overcome demons diminish their army.
Some restrict this to the vice in which the demon was defeated.
